senses.gloss:
Kharoṣṭhī
------------------------------------------
Ideas can revolutionise a whole society. But, ideas can be expressed only through the spoken word or the written word. Whereas the former can evaporate quickly, the latter can be permanently recorded. This, again, needs a script.
Out of the several ancient scripts that have come to light through archaeological or numismatical discoveries, the खरोष्ठी is also one. Considered as a Sanskrit word, it means ‘the lips (= oṣṭha) of an ass (= khara)’. It is said that uncivilised and uncultured people used to use this script in Turkistan, Tibet and Iran. Others opine that the Aramaic word ‘kharottha’ became ‘Kharoṣṭhī’ in Sanskrit.
Writings in this script have been discovered on the edicts etched on stone, metal plates, wood, hides as also on coins.
Rock inscriptions of अशोक discovered in Shabazgashi in the Peshawar district of Pakistan, in Manshera (Hazara district in Pakistan) as also the Indo-Sythian and Indo-Greek coins contain this script. It might have been existent during the period 300 B. C. to A. D. 500 in India and disappeared later on. It was common among the Bactrians, Hūṇas and Kuśānas.
It was generally written from the right to the left, though writing it the other way was not uncommon.
The खरोष्ठी script is different from the ब्राह्मी script.
See also BRĀHMĪ.
